scenarios.name: enters-prepared-without-flying-or-haste
scenarios.why: Cast for {3}{B/R} it enters as a 3/3 and prepared, so (with {B} available) a copy of Vicious Verse is offered to cast. The runner addresses that castable copy as p0:Vicious Verse. No opponent has been dealt noncombat damage this turn, so the Wordsmith has neither flying nor haste.

scenarios.name: prepared-copy-pings-opponent-and-grants-flying-haste
scenarios.why: While prepared, its controller casts a copy of Vicious Verse targeting the opponent: 1 noncombat damage (20 -> 19). An opponent has now been dealt noncombat damage this turn, so the Wordsmith has flying and haste, and it stays on the battlefield.

scenarios.name: haste-lets-it-attack-the-turn-it-enters
scenarios.why: Cast the Wordsmith, then Lightning Bolt the opponent (noncombat damage): it has haste, so it can attack the turn it came under its controller's control, dealing 3 combat damage (20 - 3 - 3 = 14).

scenarios.name: self-damage-does-not-count-and-it-ends-with-the-turn
scenarios.why: A Lightning Bolt to its own controller is not damage to an OPPONENT: still no flying or haste. After the prepared Vicious Verse copy hits the opponent it gains both, but on the opponent's turn (turn 2) no opponent has been dealt noncombat damage THIS turn, so it has neither again.

scenarios.name: prepared-copy-costs-its-mana-cost
scenarios.why: 'You may cast a copy of its spell' grants no cost exemption (contrast 'without paying its mana cost'), so casting the copy pays Vicious Verse's {B/R} (CR 601.2f). With an empty pool and no mana sources the copy is not offered; with {B} floating it is, and the cast spends that {B}.
